question: Can a globally constrained directed typed-role solver on exactly the original frozen retained memory resolve intermediate ambiguity without using a privileged answer, changing online memory policies, or accessing new cohorts?
hypothesis: Enumerating all semantically admissible combinations of stored role-segment records across the complete question, then returning an endpoint only when globally unique, may resolve F84's three isolated path ambiguity failures. The F60 and F83 equal-memory inputs must not be altered, and any online-science interpretation remains prohibited.

algorithm.input: Only current frozen retained records and query start+ordered (role,direction) operations, NEVER query answer or future public events.
algorithm.states: Directed dynamic programming states (consumed_operation_count,node_identity). For each available retained record and its exact reversal, traverse only if its encoded role/direction codes exactly equal the next query segment; no partial record matches.
algorithm.resolution: Collect all terminal node identities after consuming all ordered operations. Return a value only if there is exactly one distinct terminal node, else None. A single answer may be reached by multiple candidate decompositions.
algorithm.capacity: Persistent memory unchanged: at most twelve 12-byte records, 144 bytes. Solver may use bounded ephemeral scratch counted separately; this is not evidence of equal compute costs.
algorithm.parity: Reversing a stored record reverses code order and flips each direction bit; forbid code synthesis and any use of hidden event labels.
failure_conditions: Unknown/malformed role sequence or invalid record input
Transient computational limit exceeded: fail closed with no answer
More than one distinct terminal answer: abstain
The new solver regresses versus identical-state frozen greedy control on any observed case: classify negative, do not adjust solver after observing
Any value not reachable from the original public typed graph: invalid.

source.public_witness: Independent full-history graph answer only for offline scoring, never solver input

classification_rules.exposed_readonly_mechanism_supported: Source/trace/identity audit passes; unchanged F60 and F83 F85-global variants show no accuracy regression on either arrival regime; and at least one previously failed case becomes correct. If D4 test passes as well, report number of rescued ambiguous witnesses separately.
classification_rules.exposed_solver_mechanism_bounded: No failures in code validity but either no prospective-relevant rescues, or D4-only rescues; no scientific promotion.
classification_rules.exposed_negative: Any F60 or F83 accuracy regression, no new working solution, graph-invalid computed answer, or unaccounted computational overflow.
classification_rules.invalid: Frozen identity, source, role encoding, legal memory trace, retained byte budget, question-answer boundary, or independent public witness fails.

controls: Freeze this precode JSON as immutable blob before running source tests.
Do not change F83/F84 parent sources, frozen control weights, exposed seeds, methods, memory records or prior classifications.
All 72 online-prefix audits for F60/F83 and all legal D4 prefix audits must pass.
Independent public graph witness must show one unique answer in each exposed case, and F85 returned result must either be none or be a graph-reachable answer.
No post-result mutation of method or thresholds to claim a success; any fix after failed experiment creates a clearly distinct revision and new evidence.
No accepted-ref mutation, merge, controller dispatch, optimizer promotion or protected prospective first-use.
